meta.title: Kanji Write: Learn Kanji Stroke Order by Hand
meta.description: Practise Japanese handwriting on iPhone and iPad. Kanji Write checks the shape, position, direction and order of every stroke of 2,200+ kanji, hiragana and katakana.
meta.ogTitle: Kanji Write: every stroke is checked
meta.ogDescription: Write kanji and kana by hand. The app checks the shape, position, direction and order of each stroke.
meta.ogImageAlt: The kanji 学 written stroke by stroke next to the words Kanji Write

store.requirement: iPhone and iPad, iOS 16 or later

hero.title: Learn kanji stroke order by hand
hero.lede: Write each character with a finger or Apple Pencil. Kanji Write checks every stroke as you draw it and tells you what to fix.
hero.demoLabel: Stroke order of the kanji 学, drawn one stroke at a time
hero.screenAlt: Kanji Write home screen on iPhone with JLPT level filters, the New and Review buttons and a grid of N5 kanji

checks.title: Four checks on every stroke
checks.lede: The app compares the line you draw with a reference stroke. A stroke is accepted only when all four checks pass.

items.title: Shape
items.body: The curve of your line must follow the curve of the stroke, hooks and turns included.

items.title: Position
items.body: The stroke must sit in the correct part of the square, so the character keeps its proportions.

items.title: Direction
items.body: A stroke drawn from the wrong end is rejected, even when it looks correct.

items.title: Order
items.body: Strokes are accepted only in the correct sequence, in every practice mode.

checks.feedbackBody: When a stroke is rejected, the app tells you the reason: correct shape but wrong order, wrong direction, or wrong position. You correct that one stroke and continue.
checks.screenAlt: Practice screen that shows the message: Right shape, wrong order: that was stroke 3. Draw stroke 1 first.

try.title: Write a kanji in your browser
try.lede: Draw the strokes in order with a mouse, a finger or a pen. This demo uses the same stroke data as the app and a simplified version of its check.
try.wrongOrder: Correct shape, wrong order. Draw stroke {current} first.
try.wrongDirection: Wrong direction. Start from the other end.
try.wrongShape: Not this stroke. Follow the guide.
try.done: Complete. All {total} strokes are in order.
try.noScript: This demo needs JavaScript. The app does not.

guides.title: From tracing to writing alone
guides.lede: Select how much help you get. The app remembers the level, and it checks stroke order at every level.

items.name: Trace
items.title: Write over the full character
items.body: All strokes show as a guide. You draw over them and each one is checked.
items.screenAlt: Trace mode on iPhone with the full character shown as a grey guide and the first strokes drawn

items.name: Guided
items.title: See only the next stroke
items.body: Only the next stroke shows. You learn the sequence one step at a time.
items.screenAlt: Guided mode on iPhone with only the next stroke shown as a guide

items.name: Copy
items.title: Write with no guide
items.body: The square is empty. The character stays in view above it and you copy it.
items.screenAlt: Copy mode on iPhone with a completed character written in an empty grid

practice.title: New characters, then Review from memory
practice.lede: The Home screen has one Practice group with two buttons. You always know what to do next.

items.name: New
items.title: Learn characters you have not written
items.body: New gives you the next characters of your level with the guide level you selected.
items.screenAlt: Home screen on iPhone with the New and Review buttons in the Practice group

items.name: Review
items.title: Write from memory
items.body: Review hides the character. You see only its readings and meaning and write it from memory. Hints can show the character or the next stroke.
items.screenAlt: Review session on iPhone with the character hidden and its meaning and readings shown

points: Characters that needed a hint or a second try come first in Review.
The Review button shows how many characters wait for you.
The Progress screen shows your practice days, completed characters and the last five weeks.
practice.progressAlt: Progress screen on iPhone with practice days, completed characters and a five-week activity grid

sentences.title: Write whole words and sentences
sentences.lede: On iPad you write a full sentence, one square for each character. Each stroke of each character is checked.
points: Each sentence comes with its reading and an English translation.
Trace the characters, write them in empty squares, or write freely with no check.
The active row stays in the centre, so a resting hand does not move the page.
sentences.screenAlt: Sentence writing on iPad with a row of squares, some characters written and the next square active

ipad.title: Made for Apple Pencil
ipad.lede: The iPad layout gives the writing area the full screen. With Apple Pencil, practice feels like a paper notebook.

items.title: Apple Pencil
items.body: Write with Apple Pencil on iPad, or with a finger on iPhone and iPad.

items.title: Haptic feedback
items.body: Apple Pencil Pro gives a light tap when a stroke is accepted and when a character is complete. iPhone uses its own haptics.

items.title: Notebook
items.body: A notebook grid lets you practise freely, row after row, as on squared paper.

items.title: Sidebar layout
items.body: The sidebar holds levels and sessions. It hides when you write, so the canvas gets all the space.

ipad.homeAlt: Kanji Write on iPad with the sidebar and the kanji grid
ipad.notebookAlt: Notebook practice on iPad with rows of handwritten characters in a grid

library.title: All the kanji you must know, and all the kana
library.lede: Filter characters by JLPT level, by Japanese school grade or by kana type. Search by character, reading or English meaning.

stats.label: hiragana and katakana, with voiced forms and yōon

library.glyphsLabel: Examples of kanji and kana from the app, drawn in stroke order

more.title: Small things that help you practise each day

items.title: Works offline
items.body: All character data is in the app. It needs no internet connection.

items.title: No account, no tracking
items.body: There is no sign-up, no analytics and no advertising.

items.title: iCloud sync
items.body: Practice history syncs between your own devices through your private iCloud.

items.title: Daily kanji widget
items.body: A widget shows one kanji each day on the Home Screen or Lock Screen. Tap it to start practice.

items.title: Strictness
items.body: Select how strictly strokes are checked: normal or strict.

items.title: Your ink
items.body: Change the ink colour, the guide colours and the guide width.

items.q: How does Kanji Write check stroke order?
items.a: The app compares each stroke you draw with a reference stroke from the KanjiVG data. It checks the shape, the position, the direction and the place of the stroke in the sequence. A stroke that fails a check is rejected and the app tells you the reason.
Yes. Kanji Write is free on the App Store.
More than 2,200 kanji, which covers JLPT N5 to N1 and the kanji of Japanese elementary school grades 1 to 6, plus all hiragana and katakana with voiced forms and yōon combinations.
Yes. On iPad you can write with Apple Pencil, and Apple Pencil Pro gives haptic feedback. You can also write with a finger on iPhone and iPad.
Yes. All data is in the app. The app has no account and collects no data.

items.q: Is it good for JLPT study?
items.a: Yes. You can filter kanji by JLPT level from N5 to N1 and practise each level in order. Writing a kanji by hand helps you remember its form and its parts.

items.q: What is the difference between New and Review?
items.a: New gives you characters that you have not practised, with a guide. Review hides the character and you write it from memory from its readings and meaning. Characters you found difficult come first.

items.q: Which languages does the app have?
items.a: The app interface is in English and Japanese. Kanji meanings are in English.
An Android version is in development. Kanji Write is available now for iPhone and iPad.
